Subject: FinOptima data handling — short-log exception & next steps

Hi Anna, Tom — thanks again for taking time today. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum.

Call summary (high level):
- Primary ask: ensure Redwoods' hosted inference can meet FinOptima's PII handling rules for a pilot — specifically a 0-retention option for user PII payloads and a short-lived KV/cache window for session context (goal: 24–48 hours).
- Residency: EU data residency for persisted artifacts and keys.
- Audit & evidence: FinOptima needs SOC2 evidence plus a proposal showing what logs (access, audit, error) would still be retained and in what form.

What Redwood can offer (summary):
- Option set we discussed: 0-retention on message bodies (no storage of raw inputs after processing), ephemeral KV cache with configurable TTL (24/48/72h), and granular audit logs with PII redaction and hashing.
- EU-hosted key management and region pinning for persisted artifacts.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Marcus: provide short technical options doc that maps to the 0-retention + 48h KV profile we discussed and call out any feature gaps.
2) Monica: confirm the legal/contract language we typically use for data deletion guarantees and what evidence we can provide (SOC2 excerpt attached).
3) Anna/Tom: confirm the pilot scope and who from your side will own procurement and legal so we can loop them into the DocuSign packet.

Attachments: SOC2_Audit_Summary.pdf (attached) — high-level evidence. I'll follow up with a retention proposal PDF from Marcus.

Proposed timeline: technical deep-dive next week (Dec 9–10), legal review the following week, pilot kickoff before end of December if paperwork aligns.

Thanks —
Soojin

Thanks Soojin — good recap. A few clarifying questions from security: 

1) When you say "0-retention on message bodies," do you mean no persistent storage at all (including intermediate backups/replicas) or no long-term indexable storage? We need explicit guarantees about ephemeral disk/replica behavior and whether any transient copies could be pulled during incident response.

2) For the KV cache TTL: we lean to 48 hours but require proof-of-delete (or verifiable TTL enforcement). Can you describe how Redwood surfaces evidence that a TTL window was enforced? Audit records sufficient for our security team would be ideal.

3) For logs: we cannot accept plaintext PII in any retained logs. Are you able to provide hashed identifiers instead of raw values and restrict log retention to 90 days for the pilot?

Procurement side: Tom will own the paperwork — cc'd. We'll likely need an initial SOW that calls out the pilot scope, acceptance criteria, and data handling SLA.

Anna Weiss
Head of Security, FinOptima

On 2026-12-07, Anna Weiss <anna.weiss@finoptima.com> wrote:
> Thanks Soojin — good recap. A few clarifying questions from security: 
> 
> 1) When you say "0-retention on message bodies," do you mean no persistent storage at all (including intermediate backups/replicas) or no long-term indexable storage?

Hi Anna — quick technical response + options. Happy to take the deep-dive next week and demo the enforcement flows. Below are two practical configurations Redwood can commit to for a pilot and the tradeoffs: 

Option A — Strict ephemeral processing (recommended for max privacy):
- Inference layer operates in-memory only for request payloads; no tokenized or raw input is persisted to object storage.
- KV cache: configurable TTL; pilot: 48h in EU region. After TTL expiry, keys are removed and storage blocks cleared.
- Replicas/backups: ephemeral replicas are allowed for in-flight HA only and are non-persistent — we run a secure wipe at the storage layer on rotation.
- Audit evidence: we can produce a TTL enforcement report (hash of keys + timestamp of deletion) and S3 lifecycle logs showing object deletion events.
- Logs: access and error logs will redact PII fields by default; for identifiers we can emit salted SHA-256 hashes (salt managed by your KMS).

Limitations / notes:
- True "proof of deletion" at the hardware level (e.g., physical disk forensic) exceeds standard SaaS guarantees; we provide cryptographic deletion audit logs and lifecycle events.
- If FinOptima requires absolute zero transient copies (including in-flight HA), we'd need an on-prem or Private deployment to fully guarantee.

Option B — Short-retain with stronger observability (practical compromise):
- Message bodies stored in encrypted object storage for 48h, then lifecycle deletion; immediate redaction of detected PII fields on write.
- KV cache TTL 48h; audit logs retain only hashed identifiers for 90 days (configurable).
- Easier to support streaming and retries for high-throughput scenarios.

Attachments: redwood-retention-proposal-v2.pdf — mapping of Option A/B to our feature flags and the expected audit outputs.

Next steps (technical):
- I'll prepare a short runbook for the pilot (enforcement proofs, Salt+KMS flow, sample TTL enforcement report) ahead of the deep-dive on Dec 9.
- Monica, please confirm any legal constraints we should embed in the SOW language (e.g., maximum log retention window).

Thanks —
Marcus Lin

2) Evidence package: Marcus to deliver the TTL enforcement runbook + sample TTL enforcement report and lifecycle log snippets by EOD Dec 8 (attached to his follow-up). Monica to propose SOW language for the deletion guarantees by Dec 10.

3) Procurement: Tom — I'll send an initial SOW + DocuSign packet tomorrow with the pilot scope (30-day pilot, acceptance criteria, data handling SLA, and pricing). Please confirm the billing contact and PO workflow so we populate the SOW correctly.

4) Scheduling: Technical deep-dive proposed Dec 9 @ 10:00 CET (Marcus + Marcus engineering + Anna). Does that time work for you?

If that looks good I'll kick off the DocuSign packet and calendar invites.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.
